subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add automatic sensitive-value sanitization to final/user-visible outputs as a core security feature, or keep core limited to current log/tool/transcript/scaffolding redaction and route optional output filtering through plugin hooks?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the requested behavior changes visible output semantics, security expectations, and likely configuration defaults; automation cannot safely choose the product/security boundary or false-positive policy.

options.title: Approve narrow core output sanitization
options.body: Define an opt-in or explicitly scoped core policy using existing redaction helpers, with schema/docs/tests and clear behavior for false positives and reporting.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub
options.body: Use reply_payload_sending or message_sending hooks for optional sanitizer packages if maintainers want core to remain limited to generic delivery seams.

options.title: Keep current boundaries
options.body: Declare logs, transcripts, tool payloads, diagnostics, and internal-scaffolding cleanup as the supported core redaction boundary and close or narrow this request later.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow core output sanitization
recommendation.body: Define an opt-in or explicitly scoped core policy using existing redaction helpers, with schema/docs/tests and clear behavior for false positives and reporting.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a security-boundary decision and CODEOWNERS routes security-sensitive code, config, and docs to this owner group.
